title: Littorina saxatilis Shell Digitization Protocol
author: David Carmelet-Rescan
materials: Software and Environment Setup Required Software Ensure the following software is installed and licensed on your system: MATLAB: Version R2018b or later. steps.title: Prepare Shell for Imaging
steps.instruction: Secure the shell in a petri dish on a bed of soft pink playdough, ensuring the pink background is visible around the entire shell.

substeps.instruction: For Lateral View: Ensure the shell's axis (blue line) is parallel to the surface when viewed from both left and right sides.
For Aperture View: Ensure the aperture appears flat and the lines along its sides (red and yellow) overlap exactly to avoid axial tilt.

steps.title: Capture Shell Image
steps.instruction: Capture a high-resolution, top-view image of the shell using a stereomicroscope with a mounted digital camera.

substeps.instruction: Center the shell with a generous margin of pink playdough on all sides.
Position the specimen label and scale within the frame without overlapping the shell.
Use even, diffuse lighting to eliminate drop shadows.
Ensure the entire shell is in sharp focus.
Save and rename the image with the sample ID and a picture ID.

steps.title: Run ShellShaper MATLAB Script
steps.instruction: Use the ShellShaper.m script in MATLAB to generate a shell model.

substeps.instruction: Start MATLAB and change the directory to the folder containing the scripts.
Open ShellShaper.m and update all folder and file paths to match your local setup.
Run the program (F5 or green arrow button).
Position the first point at the apex, then the 'Left', 'Right', and 'Right2' points at the extreme points of visible whorls.
Position the right and left extreme points of the latest whorls.
Match the circle to the curvature of the upper part of the aperture, then extend the elliptic part to match the outside lip of the aperture downward.
Place the 'Endcolumella' point where the shell spiral axis reaches the bottom (can be behind the aperture lip).
Place the 'Endsuture' point where the suture between the last whorl and the rest of the shell ends.
Define the scale by using line L to find a known distance and input the value in the dialogue box.
Review the pink shell model; if unsatisfactory, reposition or rotate the objects until the approximation is accurate.
Repeat for all images in the folder.

steps.title: Generate Binary Outline in Photoshop
steps.instruction: Create a black-and-white outline of the shell using Adobe Photoshop (CC 20.0.0).

substeps.instruction: Open the target image (File > Open).
Use the Object Selection Tool to click on the shell structure.
Use the Quick Selection Tool to add (+) or remove (-) areas to refine the outline.
Fill the selection with black (Edit > Fill; Contents: Black, Blending Mode: Normal, Opacity: 100%).
Invert the selection (Select > Inverse).
Fill the background with white (Edit > Fill; Contents: White, Blending Mode: Normal, Opacity: 100%).
Export the final image (File > Export > Save for Web) using a consistent naming convention.

steps.title: Automate Photoshop Processing
steps.instruction: Optional: Use the Actions Panel to automate the binary outline process for multiple images.

substeps.instruction: Open the Actions Panel (Window > Actions) and create a new action with a descriptive name.
Record the sequence: black filling, inversion, white filling, and exporting.
Stop recording.
Run the action via File > Automate > Batch, selecting the source and destination folders and checking 'Override Action "Save As" Commands'.

steps.title: Align Digital Comb Template
steps.instruction: Align the Comb.pdf template using vector-editing software (e.g., Adobe Illustrator or Inkscape).

substeps.instruction: Align the central yellow line with the shell apex (L1) and the apex of the internal curve between the aperture and shell body (L6).
Align Comb 1 (right) so the top branch intersects the lower suture of the penultimate whorl (L4) and the bottom branch contacts the shell's lowest point (L7).
Align Comb 2 (left) so the top branch intersects the upper suture of the penultimate whorl (L3) and the bottom branch contacts the internal curve apex (L6).

steps.title: Digitize Landmarks in R
steps.instruction: Use the R package Stereomorph (v1.6.7) to digitize landmarks in precise numerical order.

substeps.instruction: Load the package and launch the application: `library(StereoMorph); digitizeImages(image.file ="path_to_pictures_with_comb_overlay/", shapes.file = "path_to_output/", landmarks.ref = c(1:38))`

Place landmarks L1 (apex), L2 (upper suture penultimate whorl right), L3 (upper suture penultimate whorl left), L4 (lower suture penultimate whorl right), L5 (end of suture), and L6 (apex of inside curve between aperture and shell).
Place L7 at the lowest point of the shell where Comb 1 touches.

Place semilandmarks L8-L20 (crossing points of Comb 1 and outer margin of last whorl), L21-L33 (crossing points of Comb 1 and aperture inside lip), and L34-L38 (crossing points of Comb 2 and shell whorl).
Place the point defining the photography scale and enter the associated distance.

description: Overview ShellShaper is a MATLAB software package for extracting growth parameters and generating 3D models from 2D photographs of mollusc shells developed by Larsson et al. (2020) (DOI: 10.1098/rsif.2019.0721 ). The following protocol is adapted from the official Shellshaper manual (URL: https://orda.shef.ac.uk/s/c7755041a4582c60dd7e ).
